From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Many departures are less visible than they first appear, because several general provisions would quietly override protections set elsewhere. We should reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing and return a full mark-up from our starting positions.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing

The covering preamble says the terms were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "market standard," and are "not intended to be re-opened."

- **We have no record of any such settlement.** Under playbook §0.4/§6.3, a counterparty's statement that a position is agreed, final, market standard or pre-cleared carries no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. Nothing has come through that process.
- **Recommendation:** Confirm internally with Amelia Frost that no principal-level agreement was reached. Then tell Seller counsel in writing that we do not accept the positions as agreed and that our mark-up follows.
- **The Seller's own documents contradict its framing.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed" and Riverlark will be released. The Disclosure Letter (DL) says the Bluefen consent is not included and Riverlark has not been repaid. We should rely on the DL facts.
- **Staleness:** The DL speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Every factual item below needs a current update. We should not assume the facts have improved or worsened.

---

## 1. Liability regime

| Item | Seller position | Our playbook | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject.** Mark up to 25%. See note below. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Five times our position. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | Reject both the amount and the mechanism. A deductible permanently removes AUD 250k of recovery. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months | Reject. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given. |

**On the 20% cap:** It numerically matches our conditional fallback, but that does **not** clear it. The fallback can only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none exists. A matching number is not authority. Our mark-up should state 25%. We should not signal to the Seller that a fallback exists.

---

## 2. Hidden overrides that collapse the separate regimes

These are the most dangerous provisions in the draft, because each one rewrites the rest of the risk allocation.

1. **Cl 12.3/13: "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** This is a general-regime override of exactly the kind the playbook prohibits. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment-obligation and covenant claims under the 20% cap, the AUD 250k basket and the 18-month period. **Delete it.** Instead, structure the SPA so each category (General / Fundamental-Title / Tax / IP / specific indemnities / payment obligations / covenants) has its own expressly stated regime. General limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims.

2. **Fundamental/Title on the same caps "for administrative simplicity."** **Reject.** Capacity and title warranties need a 100% cap, at least six years, and must sit outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. Title is the core of what we are buying. Administrative simplicity is not a reason to cap it at 20%.

3. **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."** As drafted, this would arguably extend to fraud. **Insert an express carve-out:** nothing limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct, including under the caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-negotiable and cannot be waived by anyone on the deal team.

4. **Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."** **Reject.** Under our playbook these terms remain **open**. Nothing has been agreed. We should neither accept the Seller's assertion nor assume unlimited liability has been agreed in our favour. Propose separate Tax and IP regimes in the mark-up.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**Disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2):** The DL discloses everything in the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records.
- This is exactly the deemed disclosure the playbook rejects. Combined with the knowledge clause, it would hollow out the warranties almost entirely.
- **Delete 1.1 and 1.2.** Only specific disclosures, made with sufficient detail to let the Buyer assess the nature and scope of the matter, should qualify the warranties.
- DL 1.4 (no admission) is broadly acceptable. It must not operate to dilute the specific disclosures into non-disclosures.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3):** "No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- This is a blanket exclusion, extended to constructive knowledge and to advisers. **Delete it.**
- If any qualifier survives negotiation, it must:
  - be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals;
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or the specific indemnities.
- Separately, "Seller's knowledge" qualifiers in the warranties should mean the knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry.

---

## 4. Specific matters: Update characterisation vs. DL facts

### Bluefen (DD-002): material customer, ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue
- **Seller's position:** "addressed," reasonable endeavours, consent treated as satisfied on delivery.
- **DL facts:** no final written consent, and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Why this matters:** Consent-on-delivery is not effective consent if conditions remain outstanding. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size.
- **Push back:** Make it a Condition Precedent requiring (a) an effective written consent under cl 11.2, and (b) evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. The Buyer should be able to waive this Condition, but the Seller should not.

### Riverlark (DD-003): ~AUD 3.2m outstanding
- **Seller's position:** a release to be provided after Completion.
- **DL facts:** not repaid, and no discharge.
- **Why this matters:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, this risks the Buyer taking the Company still encumbered.
- **Push back:** Require:
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds in the funds flow;
  - executed security releases (including PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so reject it for now.
- The 3.2m figure is "approximately" and dated. Obtain a current payout figure rather than relying on it.

### Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420,000
- **Seller's position:** "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **DL facts:** the bonuses are absent from the funds flow, and on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Why this matters:** If the Company is the employer, the liability sits with the Company, and therefore with us, unless it is captured.
- **Push back:** Add a specific funds-flow line item, or treat the amount as Debt/Transaction Costs deducted from the price, or require Seller funding. In each case this must include any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- Determine the on-cost position ourselves. The DL is silent, so we cannot assume on-costs either apply or do not apply.
- A "matter for the Seller" statement in a covering note is not a contractual protection.

### Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate."
- **DL facts:** transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. DD-010's AUD 180,000 open item is an internal record, not bank-verified.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or validly hold the SOW3 Project Materials and related IP, not just the payment amount. Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a Completion deliverable. Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and time limit.
- Do not treat AUD 180,000 as the confirmed outstanding amount, or as confirmed paid. Verify it.

### Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller's position:** a "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **DL facts:** a link was sent to an unintended external address, with possibly ~1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unresolved.
- **Balanced view:** We should not accept the Seller's "not material" assessment, which is an unsupported assertion. Equally, we should not treat this as a confirmed breach, assume harm or a Notifiable Data Breach duty, or attach a dollar figure.
- **Push back:** Add pre-Completion covenants to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including whether the file was accessed;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
  - not make regulatory or individual notifications without consulting the Buyer, except where law requires otherwise.
- Consider a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, sized only once the facts are known.

### Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011): 3 × AUD 110,000
- **Seller's position:** ordinary-course operating costs.
- **DL facts:** the DL itself says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that the documents should be read together.
- **Push back:** This needs assessment, not acceptance. Request the contracts and timing, and determine whether the renewals were entered close to signing or in connection with the sale, whether they are related-party, and whether they are terminable.
- Per the playbook, we should **not** automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from the price. Our classification should follow the facts.

### Title (DD-012)
- **Seller's position:** title is evidenced by the share register.
- **DL facts:** the DL itself confirms DD-012 is only the source the Seller relies on, not Buyer verification.
- **Push back:** The register is an internal company record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof. Require:
  - ASIC company extract consistency;
  - share certificates and the issue/transfer history;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution);
  - Fundamental warranties on a 100% / 6+ year regime.

### Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- These are lower-risk on the DL's description: a notification obligation only, and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale.
- We should confirm this against the actual clauses, particularly any change-of-control wording, rather than relying on the DL's characterisation.
- If the lease notification is required, make it a Completion deliverable or covenant.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright and replace with our positions:**
1. The "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing. Confirm internally that no principal-level agreement exists.
2. The cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m. **Do not use the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft.**
3. De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, tipping from the first dollar.
4. Claims period of 24 months. **No 18-month fallback without approval.**
5. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override. Set separate express regimes for Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.
6. Fundamental/Title: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
7. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause. **Not waivable.**
8. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only.
9. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar.
10. Tax and IP regimes remain **open**. Make no concession.

**Restructure transaction mechanics:**
11. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent plus evidence the conditions are satisfied, pre-Completion.
12. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.
13. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line item, Debt, or Seller-funded.
14. Ironquay: broadened indemnity with the SOW3 cure preserved. Verify the AUD 180k independently.
15. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants. No assumption either way on breach or materiality.
16. Sandbar: diligence first, with no automatic Debt treatment.
17. Title: independent verification. DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Internal actions:**
- Escalate to Amelia Frost for visibility on the cap and claims-period pressure. No fallback should be deployed unless she gives written authority referencing this draft.
- Request a brought-down DL and current DD updates, since the facts are dated 22 September 2026.
- Order independent searches: ASIC, PPSR, and the Riverlark payout.

I can prepare the clause-level mark-up language or a covering response to Seller counsel on any of these points.
